text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Speculation National Australia Bank is preparing a takeover worth more than A$2 billion has increased after a broking house favoured by NAB bought almost six percent of St George Bank yesterday. The raid forced St George's share price up to A$9.05 and came shortly after St George announced it would not hold a shareholders meeting to approve its A$2.65 billion bid for Advance Bank. Page 1.

The world's second largest software company, Computer Associates, shuts its e-mail off for four hours a day and part of the Victorian government is considering doing the same because of the working hours wasted processing e-mail. Computer Associates' general manager of operations, Gary Mitchell, said the company found people were more likely to get on with business by communicating face to face. Page 1.

The latest Australian Bureau of Statistics housing approval figures indicate the private housing sector may be ready to turn a corner, with dwellings approvals falling 8.6 percent in seasonally adjusted terms in September - a slump caused entirely by a drop in approvals for "other" private dwellings, such as units and apartments. Page 5.

Lion Nathan chief executive Douglas Myers yesterday announced a 25.7 percent slump in profits in the year to August 31 and revealed the trans-Tasman brewer's market share had slipped 1.4 percent to 42 percent compared to Foster's 56 percent share. Lion Nathan will release a new premium brand beer in Australia next week in an effort to win back market share from its arch rival. Page 31.

Despite Premier Oil yesterday raising its bid for oil producer Discovery Petroleum from 70 cents to 80 cents a share, the board of Discovery rejected the new offer claiming it still undervalued the shares. Directors will review the offer next week, keeping in mind Grant Samuel's independent valuation of the company's shares, which valued them at between 77 cents and 95 cents each. Page 31.

The board of Aristocrat Leisure Ltd is now equally balanced between Ainsworth family members and non-family and has just one independent director following the election of Simon and Paul Ainsworth to the board yesterday in place of Geoffrey Ainsworth and independent director Frank Burke. Page 32.
THE AUSTRALIAN

After reaching social and environmental agreements with indigenous groups and government authorities of Canada's remote Northwest Territories, BHP and joint-venture partner Dia Met Minerals of Canada appear close to securing Canadian Government approval for the A$1.23 billion Lac de Gras diamond project which the partners predict will produce about five million carats of high-grade gem diamonds a year. Page 25.

Yesterday's Aristocrat Leisure Industries Ltd annual meeting produced a board shake-up which saw the appointment of Ainsworth family members Paul and Simon to the gaming machine manufacturer's board and the sacking of non-executive director Frank Burke an another Ainsworth brother, Geoff. Page 25.

A recent research report suggests Foster's Brewing Group Ltd could be subject to a takeover by Dutch beer giant Heineken. Senior brewing sources claimed yesterday that the Dutch group had participated in discussions earlier this year about the future ownership of Foster's. Questioned about who was more likely to see an ownership change in the near future, Lion Nathan Ltd chief executive Doug Myers said yesterday that Foster's was a more likely candidate. Page 25.

Lion Nathan Ltd chief executive Douglas Myers expressed disappointment at the trans-Tasman brewer's overall result yesterday, after announcing a 27 percent fall in annual profit from NZ$214.3 million to NZ$155.5 million. However, Myers said progress had been made with the group's growing commitment to China and further debt repayments of NZ$146 million had been completed. Page 27.

Following St George Bank Ltd's announcement yesterday that it would not hold a shareholders' meeting on its proposed A$2.6 billion takeover of Advance Bank Ltd, Australian Shareholders Association executive officer Tony McLean said an attempt by shareholdrs to hold an alternative public meeting was highly likely. Page 27.

North Ltd chairman Michael Deeley conceded yesterday at the company's annual meeting in Sydney that 1996/97 would be another year of flat trading as the company moves towards sustained growth from 1998. Deeley partially blamed a number of setbacks for the company's plight, including the New South Wales Government's decision not to approve the Lake Cowal gold mine and the death of hundreds of birds at the Northparkes gold and copper mine. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Despite demands from big and small shareholders for a vote on its planned A$2.65 billion takeover of Advance Bank, St George Bank will risk a shareholder revolt after announcing yesterday it had been granted an exemption from holding a meeting to approve the deal by the Australian Stock Exchange. Page 21.

Following a report from the government's Indicative Planning Council forecasting a slow grinding increase in housing activity, building approvals have experienced their sharpest fall in two years, dropping nine percent in September. Reacting to the news, building materials stocks slipped. Page 21.

Institutional investors will be asked next week to express interest in buying John Singleton Advertising's 10 percent voting stake in the Ten Group. JSA plans to sell its shares through a listed unit trust which fellow Ten shareholders Robert Whyte and Jack Cowin have also agreed to use when they sell their shareholdings. Page 21.

A decline in Australian earnings and revenues and a significantly increased tax charge helped prompt a 26 percent slump in Lion Nathan's net profit for the year to August 31, from NZ$202.3 million to NZ$150.4 million, but the brewer revealed yesterday it was moving to refocus its Australian operations to win back market share from Carlton & United Breweries. Page 21.

Although National Foods posted marginally better results for the first quarter and is budgeted for an improved profit for the 1997 financial year, chairman Barry Capp told shareholders at yesterday's annual general meeting that tough economic conditions would force the company to focus on cost savings and efficiency gains throughout the year. Page 23.

Seven Network managing director Gary Rice said yesterday the group's planned 43 job cuts around Australia were designed to streamline the network and help it concentrate resources on its on-screen image. Thirty-three of the retrenchments will come from the Sydney station, with the remainder coming from Melbourne and Perth. Page 23.
THE AGE

Recent gloomy economic news may soon prompt the Reserve Bank to cut interest rates significantly to stimulate the economy. Figures indicate a sharp drop in housing approvals, plummeting demand for skilled workers and a flat rate of total hours worked. Data recorded by The Economist reveals real estate interest rates in Australia are 4.6 percent compared with an average of 2.1 percent in the rest of the West. Page C1.

Cigarette brands represented five out of the 10 top-selling items in Australian supermarkets in the 12 months to June 1996, with supermarkets increasing their share of cigarette sales by taking market share from other retailers, according to a survey of Australia's Top 100 Grocery Brands released today by Nielsen Australia, in conjunction with Ad News. Page C1.

Geological Survey of Victoria manager Tom Dickson told the Mining Week conference in Melbourne yesterday that the Victorian gold industry has added nearly four million ounces of gold to its resource base in the past three years - an addition of A$1.9 billion in revenue terms. Page C1.

Fierce competition from Carlton & United Breweries and a A$20 million downturn in Australian beer revenues forced Lion Nathan's net earnings for the year to August 31 down 26 percent from NZ$202.3 million to NZ$150.4 million. Lion's share of the Austraian beer market dropped from 43.4 percent to 42 percent. Page C3.

Amid speculation that National Australia Bank is increasing its strategic holding in St George Bank after NAB's usual broker purchased 675,000 shares in the bank yesterday, St George has been granted an exemption from holding a shareholders meeting on itsA$2.65 billion takeover of Advance Bank. Page C3.

After reporting a net profit of A$15.1 million in 1996 on revenue of A$1.154 billion, National Foods chairman Barry Capp told the annual meeting in Sydney that National Foods would have to focus on cost savings and efficiency gains to survive the tough economic conditions ahead. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
